$comment: The world's voxel grids (docs/proposals/MOON_WORLD.md): every buildable two-faced disc a world has, each with its own frame (where it sits and how it turns: `rest` is the home world, the grid everything else is placed against; `orbit` follows the sky's moon path, docs/DAY_NIGHT.md; `sunPath` sits on the sky's sun path at daynight.json `sun.distanceM`, its face A toward home, docs/proposals/SUN_WORLD.md), its disc radius (`radiusM`, or `world` for the world's own size, docs/proposals/BIG_MAP.md), its seed (`seedSalt` mixed into the world seed; none keeps the world seed), its surface gravity (`gravityScale` × the home world's), the distance from its centre inside which a flying player is captured into its frame (`captureM`, moving grids only) and the distance past which it is drawn as a far body from its baked maps (`farM`), how high its ground reaches over its midplane (`surfaceM`, far flight's slab), whether it has air (`atmosphere`, none unless declared: the day sky is a layer over space that thins with height, docs/DAY_NIGHT.md §15; without, the sky is space at every hour, the night sky's: the moon, the sun), the coarse mesh of its surface drawn from another grid nearer than `farM` (`nearMesh`: `cells` quads across its diameter, each vertex the lowest ground round it less `sinkM`; MOON_WORLD.md §7.3 M-5), or at every distance when the sky draws no disc of it (`skyDisc` false: home, seen from the moon, M-6), the distant terrain drawn past its chunks while on it (`lod`: `levels` square rings centred on the viewer, `cells` quads a side, level k's quads `cellM` × 2^k wide, each vertex its ground less `sinkM` + `sinkPerCell` × the quad's width so the chunks cover it, reaching past its disc's radius; BUGS.md #143, #145), and what lights its ground while on it (`light`; none for home, lit by the sky's keyframes; BUGS.md #145): `sunlit` (the sun's light, its keyframes' turned into the grid's frame; false on the sun, which lights nothing inside it), the `bodies` that light it by the sunlight they reflect (at most 2: another grid by name, its `albedo` colour and its linear `intensity` when seen full at `refDeg` in angular radius; at a moment × the share of its disc lit as seen from the viewer, its phase, × (its angular radius / `refDeg`)², toward its true direction), the least `ambient` light (a colour × `min`) and a `glow` from its own ground lighting surfaces from below (the sun's lava: a colour × `intensity`) and the capability a client must say to be captured into it (`capability`, optional: a client without it flies on through and sees the grid as a far body; the sun's `grid.sun`, docs/proposals/SUN_WORLD.md §5), its generator by kind (`terrain`: today's home generator, crates/dwell-worldgen TerrainGenerator; `cratered`: the moon rules below; `volcanic`: the sun's, below). Heights are face-local metres (+y up from the grid's midplane, the same frame as the home terrain's), and each face is generated from its own seed stream like the home world's (bifacial::face_seed). Read by crates/dwell-worldgen/src/grids.rs, which validates every entry with a message. The content is prototype (ARCHITECTURE.md §6.1).

travel.$comment: Travel between the grids (MOON_WORLD.md §7). Far flight (creative flight in space; owner 2026-11-13: "a much faster fly speed for creative. But only in space."): farther than `aboveM` from every grid's slab (its disc, `surfaceM` thick each side of its midplane) a flier goes at least `perS` × that distance m/s (easing down toward every body's surface), up to `maxMps` × how far into space it is (the atmosphere's thinning, the sky's value, docs/DAY_NIGHT.md §15: none in home's air, all of it in space), so the moon's ~597 km take about 35 s and the speed falls smoothly toward either surface. A player captured inside a grid's `captureM` is released past `captureM` × `releaseFactor`.

generator.$comment: The home world's far bake (MOON_WORLD.md §5, M-6) is made from its world map: heights and water from the map's cells, the colour from each column's surface block (its biome's palette, blocks.json `color`). `bake.size` is its texels a side per face (256: 390 m texels over the 50 km disc).

Cratered plains over a datum, ridged noise for the ridges, maria as smooth low basins (fewer craters, flatter, and their ground `maria.block`, a darker dust: a column is the mare's block where it is at least half in a mare, `block` elsewhere; the far bake's colour is each block's `color`, blended by how far in a mare a texel is), and a crater field of size classes, each `perKm2` craters a km² with radii drawn in `radiusM`. Heights never go under `minM` (the grid's floor over its midplane, where overlapping craters would dig through). A crater's profile, by radius R: a floor `depthRatio` × R deep (at most `maxDepthM`) flat over `floorFraction` of R, a bowl up to a rim `rimRatio` × R high (at most `maxRimM`) at R, and ejecta falling off as the cube of the distance out to `reach` × R. `ramps` is the rule that shapes its tops into the ground blocks' stored ramps (docs/HALF_HEIGHT_GRID.md §4, §10: `none`, `strict` or `notched`; BUGS.md #144). `bake.size` is the far-LOD map's texels a side per face.

The sun as a volcano world (docs/proposals/SUN_WORLD.md, WORK_QUEUE item 42; owner 2026-11-12: "The sun is a volcano world. Constant flowing lava, oceans of lava."). Face-local heights over its midplane, each face from its own seed stream. The ground is `datumM` + fbm `plains` + broad fbm `basins`; wherever it lies under `lava.seaM` it is a lava ocean's floor, lava (`lava.fluid`, the lava fields' block) up to that level. Rifts follow ridged noise's zero lines, carved `rifts.depthM` deep across `width` of the noise's range, their bottom `fill` of that depth a lava river (its surface follows the land, so it runs downhill). Cones: one candidate a jittered `cones.cellM` cell (`chance`), radius and height drawn in their ranges, the flank `(1 - d/R)^profile` over the ground at its centre, a summit crater `craterRatio` x R wide and `craterDepthM` deep holding a lava lake `lakeBelowRimM` under its rim. The ground is `crust` (basalt), and a dry column at most `shore.bandM` over the lava it borders is `shore.block` (obsidian, the quench glass). Heights never go under `minM`. `flow` keeps its rivers running (the server's lava fields, below). `bake.size` is the far bake's texels a side per face (the sky's sun disc is drawn from face A's).

flow.$comment: Constant flowing lava (owner, 2026-11-12; SUN_WORLD.md §6): the server's lava fields (VOLCANOES.md, the same flow, hardening, burn and damage as home's) kept running on the sun's rivers. One source a `cellM` cell at its river head (of `probes` x `probes` samples, the one with the highest river lava: at least `minRift` in a rift, molten, over the sea, not a crater's lake), a `vent` of `fluid` at `rateM3s` whose field starts `radius` columns each way. Bounded as the water is: sources are placed only within `nearM` of a player on the sun, at most `maxFields` fields (the farthest from every player dropped first), each grown to at most `maxTiles` tiles of 8 x 8 columns, and a field with no player within lava.json `nearRadiusM` of it is not run (no fast-forward: a steady river).
